summary: Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi was an Indologist and historian who earned his BA at Deccan College and a PhD from the University of Mumbai. He served as Principal of Morris College and Vidarbha Mahavidyalaya, and later held chairmanships and professorships at Nagpur University.

Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow. He served as Curator of the Government Museum, Mathura, Director of the State Museum, Lucknow, and Head of Indology at BHU.

Vasudha Dalmia is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Delhi, University of Cologne, JNU, and Heidelberg University. Her career includes teaching at the University of Tübingen, UC Berkeley, Free University of Berlin, and Yale University.

Vasudha Narayanan is a religious studies scholar and Indologist who studied at the University of Madras, University of Mumbai, and Harvard University. She became Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida and served as president of the American Academy of Religion.

Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Manikya Shastri and Martanda Dikshit, earning PhDs from Central Sanskrit University and National Sanskrit University. He held posts at JRRSU and Karnataka Samskrit University.

Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indologist who studied at Sir C.R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University. He served as Associate Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and held visiting professorships at Chicago and Emory.

Vempati Kutumba Sastry is an Indologist who served as Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University from 2003 to 2008. He also served as president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies and was a board member of the Wider Association of Vedic Studies.

Ven. Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti, having also studied under traditional teacher Bhante Dhammasakkaro.

Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge. She held research fellowships at St Edmund's College and St Hilda's College, lectured at King's College London, and became Professor of Philosophy and Classics at Yale University in 2006.

Verrier Elwin was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who was educated at Dean Close School and Merton College. From circa 1945 to 1949, he served as the first deputy director of the Anthropological Survey of India.

Vesna Wallace is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed her doctoral dissertation at UC Berkeley. She held the Numata Chair in Buddhist Studies at the University of Oxford until 2010 and served as a professor at UC Santa Barbara.

Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who earned his BA at Yale University and his PhD at SOAS University of London. In 1984, he was appointed Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History at the University of Michigan.

Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago. In 2005, he founded the Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education and served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia.

Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from Temple University in 2004. He served as Assistant Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Albright College, attested in 2007.

Victor H. Mair was a sinologist and linguist who studied at Dartmouth, SOAS, and Harvard. He was an assistant professor at Harvard before becoming a professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 1979 and a fellow at the Swedish Collegium.

Victor Henry was a French linguist and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Douai, the University of Lille, and the École Centrale de Lille, and in 1888 became professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at the University of Paris.

Victor Turner was an anthropologist and religious studies scholar educated at UCL and the University of Manchester. He held positions at the Rhodes-Livingstone Institute, Manchester, Cornell University, the University of Chicago, and the University of Virginia.
Victoria Sujata is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Harvard University, where she studied under Michael Aris.

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held positions at Visva-Bharati University, serving as a collation supervisor and later Principal, and served as the Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta.

Vidya Dehejia is an art historian and Indologist who studied at St. Xavier's College, Newnham College, and the University of Cambridge. She served as chief curator at the Smithsonian Institution and as a professor of Indian art at Columbia University.
